Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue has a multiplicative inverse.

First note that no \(a_n\) is \(0\). Indeed, \(a_0=1\), and if \(a_n\not\equiv 0\), then \(a_{n+1}\equiv 0\) would make the given congruence become
\[
0\equiv a_n,
\]
a contradiction. Thus all \(a_n\) are invertible modulo \(397\).

From
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]
multiply by \(a_n^{-1}a_{n+1}^{-1}\):
\[
a_{n+1}^{-1}\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+a_n^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]
Rearranging gives
\[
a_n\equiv a_{n+1}^{-1}-a_n^{-1}-2\pmod{397}.
\]

Sum this from \(n=0\) to \(2025\):
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2025} a_n
\equiv a_{2026}^{-1}-a_0^{-1}-2\cdot 2026
\pmod{397}.
\]
Since \(a_0=1\) and \(a_{2026}=9\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2025} a_n
\equiv 9^{-1}-1-4052\pmod{397}.
\]

Now
\[
9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\pmod{397},
\]
so
\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\pmod{397}.
\]
Also
\[
4052=10\cdot 397+82\equiv 82\pmod{397}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2025} a_n
\equiv 353-1-82=270\pmod{397}.
\]

Finally, add \(a_{2026}=9\):
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n\equiv 270+9=279\pmod{397}.
\]

Thus the required remainder is

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
